tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)
units.summary: State what is meant by electronegativity.

units.label: 1(b)(i)
units.summary: Complete a diagram of hydrogen bonding between two water molecules with dipoles and lone pairs.

units.label: 1(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why water molecules are polar.

units.label: 1(b)(iii)
units.summary: Explain why ice is less dense than water.

units.label: 1(c)(i)
units.summary: Suggest why solid ammonia melts at a lower temperature than ice.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar comparison of hydrogen bond strength and number

units.label: 1(c)(ii)
units.summary: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of the ammonium ion.

units.label: 1(c)(iii)
units.summary: Outline a test for ammonium ions including observations.

units.label: 1(d)
units.summary: Calculate mass of anhydrous zinc sulfate from heating hydrated zinc sulfate.
units.difficulty_basis: Standard multi-step water of crystallisation calculation

units.label: 2(a)(i)
units.summary: Complete electron configurations and blocks for Be, F, Mg and Cl.

units.label: 2(a)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why electron configuration is an example of a periodic trend.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs articulation of repeating pattern from data

units.label: 2(a)(iii)
units.summary: Explain why Mg forms 2+ ions and Cl forms 1- ions.
units.difficulty_basis: Links electron configuration to ion charge

units.label: 2(a)(iv)
units.summary: Write the equation for magnesium reacting with oxygen.

units.label: 2(b)(i)
units.summary: Explain in terms of electron transfer why calcium with HCl is redox.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs both oxidation and reduction in electron terms

units.label: 2(b)(ii)
units.summary: Show by calculation that calcium is in excess of HCl and explain why it all reacts.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar twist needing recall of Ca with water

units.label: 2(c)(i)
units.summary: Add missing points for B and Mg to a first ionisation energy graph.
units.difficulty_basis: Applies trend and group 2 to 3 reasoning to graph

units.label: 2(c)(ii)
units.summary: Write an equation with state symbols for the second ionisation energy of boron.

units.label: 3(a)
units.summary: State what is meant by enthalpy change of reaction.

units.label: 3(b)
units.summary: Calculate an enthalpy change from calorimetry data and state assumptions and improvements.
units.difficulty_basis: Six-mark levels response combining calculation and evaluation

units.label: 3(c)
units.summary: Explain why halving the solution volume leaves the enthalpy change unchanged.
units.difficulty_basis: Requires proportional reasoning about q and moles

units.label: 4(a)
units.summary: Use a Boltzmann distribution to explain how a catalyst increases rate.

units.label: 4(b)(i)
units.summary: Draw a best-fit curve through gas volume data and circle the anomaly.

units.label: 4(b)(ii)
units.summary: Find rate at 50 s from a tangent to a volume-time graph.

units.label: 4(b)(iii)
units.summary: Calculate hydrogen peroxide concentration needed to give 90 cm3 of oxygen at RTP.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step with stoichiometric ratio and unit conversion

units.label: 4(c)
units.summary: Suggest two variables to control when comparing catalysts.

units.label: 5(a)
units.summary: Draw products of but-1-ene with bromine, hydrogen and steam.
units.difficulty_basis: Four structures including mixture of products

units.label: 5(b)(i)
units.summary: Outline the electrophilic addition mechanism of but-1-ene with HBr.
units.difficulty_basis: Four-mark mechanism with curly arrows and dipoles

units.label: 5(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why 2-bromobutane is the major product.
Deduce the structure of compound X from composition, mass spectrum and IR spectrum.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended six-mark integration of several data sources
